fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "A Mental Game Learned the Hard Way", "body": "Sepano Zadeh traces his path to age fourteen or so, when he took up subliminal messaging and worked with the subconscious mind, pointing to Bruce Lipton's biology of belief and epigenetics as the heart of it. He recalls being strong on the tennis court but unable to carry that into matches, which he reads as something lacking on the mental side. Martial arts after college became the next chapter, and he describes his book The Art of the Fight as the distillation of sixteen years of self-enhancement."}, {"title": "Color, Number and Subtle Energy", "body": "Chance wonders aloud whether color and small choices matter, mentioning radionics talk of a toxic lime green, which he is careful to say is what others claim. Sepano answers that he practices qigong daily as his energy work and notices forces the five senses miss. He adds that he follows Pythagorean numerology, where a universal day and a personal day interact, and calls a five day the energy of the unexpected. Chance offers that Friday is Venus's day, so a five day and a Phi day at once."}, {"title": "One Flow Behind Many Names", "body": "Chance passes along a researcher he respects, Michael Tsarion, who holds that Hermeticism came from the East, and describes the Tao as a single flow that only seems divided by our vantage points. Sepano agrees that naming is arbitrary, since the Tao is the way and the way cannot be named, and he sees the same single source in Hermeticism, in Walter Russell's writing on light and in the seven Hermetic principles, which he calls master keys. He adds that any art form can quietly tap into that oneness."}, {"title": "Art, Artifice and the Trap of Words", "body": "Chance argues that one small word does too much work: art names both the healing and creative arts and the root of artificial, and lawyers, doctors and scientists use terms of art that wall people off from each other. In his view, expressions of imagination that harmonize with nature are not artificial, and people who conclude that art is bad miss finding and expressing their own. He wants cleaner distinctions in language, and Sepano answers with the Hermetic principle of polarity and its double-edged sword."}, {"title": "Cause, Effect and the Pendulum", "body": "Sepano brings in the Hermetic principle of rhythm and a line he attributes to the Kybalion, that the adept polarizes above the swing of the pendulum, using law against law. Chance turns that into a hurdle he can jump, and Sepano pictures Mario with his cape flying over obstacles, the one who is cause instead of effect. They land on not blaming others and on taking responsibility, and Sepano adds that qigong, in his experience, opens subtle senses and that imagination is the tool of the mind."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Sepano Zadeh is a martial artist and coach who specializes in mental training techniques that improve physical performance results. Join us to hear about how to aim for your goal, resonate in your flow, and fine tune your process to embody your unlimited nature, with a warrior's mindset.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The ART System in Three Stages", "body": "Sepano explains that ART stands for aiming, resonating and tuning, each with three sub phases: attention, awareness and action; realization, revelation and rise; technique, training and triumph. He frames them as the what, the why and the how, and calls triumph both a state and an outcome, the state mattering more. Chance recognizes the shape of the trivium and, in his own reading, the three swirls of the Tao, and hears a way to teach that old pattern in practical terms."}, {"title": "Resonating and the Power Within", "body": "In the resonating stage Sepano says the point is to realize who you are by asking what you love and what you care for, because in his view deeper trouble comes from living out of line with that inner truth. He says the grander the purpose, the less limited the potential, and urges people to remember who they were before being told otherwise. Chance compares the practice to striking a tuning fork again and again, and later says finding selfhood does not feel like a choice but like the best choice."}, {"title": "Winning and Learning, Stops and Falls", "body": "Asked how to feel triumph after losing the metaphorical match, Sepano answers that there is no absolute defeat, only winning and learning, a phrase he says he first heard from Paul Chek. He separates stops, where you reflect and return to the drawing board, from falls, which he treats as true defeat. He and Chance agree through Mario and cheat codes that a story or game with no setback would hold no fun, and Sepano says he would rather earn it."}, {"title": "Portals, Imagination and Consent", "body": "Sepano describes human beings as portals with unlimited potential, and says the collective plays out whatever game the masses consent to. Chance carries the idea further, calling imagination the portal one can step through internally to any when or what, and says the difference between creative and non-creative people is deciding the next step on the canvas instead of asking to be told what to do. Sepano adds that the non-artist waits on conditions or permission, and that gifts can turn into curses, so discernment matters, pointing to self-love versus self-obsession."}, {"title": "Simple Practice and the Empty Vessel", "body": "On qigong, Sepano advises starting simple by pairing breath with movement, using imagination and intention, and he describes his own short sessions woven into daily life. Chance adds that he lowers the bar so showing up counts as victory. Sepano calls the ego a tool and desire its muscle, a double-edged sword. Chance's image is the jar emptied of what does not belong, where he says enlightenment is a destructive process and spirit attracts toward emptiness, a thought Sepano affirms."}]

fields.Quotes JSON: [{"text": "When we learn how to master one aspect of self, it shows us the path to master any other aspect of self.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Whether it's martial arts or music or painting, dancing, whatever it is, singing, it's like you're tapping into the Tao, you're tapping into the way without even knowing it.", "author": "Sepano Zadeh", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ee2bb4db-feef-4a00-8649-8444e3c20ad2/SEPANO-ZADEH.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "When our arts, if you will, our expressions from our imagination are in harmony with nature, they're not artificial.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "You're not giving a power away by blaming other things outside of you, which again makes you effect and not cause.", "author": "Sepano Zadeh", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ee2bb4db-feef-4a00-8649-8444e3c20ad2/SEPANO-ZADEH.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "The practice of qigong goes way, way beyond just the physical benefits. It's a way of tapping into that subtle energy, the things that you can't pick up with the five physical senses.", "author": "Sepano Zadeh", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ee2bb4db-feef-4a00-8649-8444e3c20ad2/SEPANO-ZADEH.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "In my opinion, imagination is exactly what Tao is.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}, {"text": "Facts and perceptions come from the realm of imagination. We can't call something what it is without first imagining it.", "author": "Sepano Zadeh", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/ee2bb4db-feef-4a00-8649-8444e3c20ad2/SEPANO-ZADEH.jpg?content-type=image%2Fjpeg"}, {"text": "You can kind of drop needing to motivate yourself with the motor of desire and let yourself be filled with your own spiritual energy and then let that be what takes you places.", "author": "Chance Garton", "portrait": "https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/5987d897cf81e0278ec5322e/aa717e55-9487-4255-a7df-3f8ef10940c4/Chance+Garton+Patreon+Portrait.png?content-type=image%2Fpng"}]
